description: Modelling data ordered in time and forecasting it with honest uncertainty: trend, seasonality and cycles, smoothing and decomposition, exponential smoothing, stationarity and autocorrelation, ARIMA and seasonal ARIMA models, regression with time series, and rigorous forecast evaluation. Every model is fitted and diagnosed in browser notebooks on real series such as rainfall in northern Ghana, food prices in Kumasi and electricity demand, and judged only by out-of-sample accuracy.
modelledOn: Hyndman and Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice
Box, Jenkins, Reinsel and Ljung, Time Series Analysis: Forecasting and Control
Shumway and Stoffer, Time Series Analysis and Its Applications
Brockwell and Davis, Introduction to Time Series and Forecasting
outcomes: Identify the trend, seasonal, cyclical and irregular components of a time series and decompose it with classical and STL methods.
Produce forecasts with benchmark methods and exponential smoothing models, including prediction intervals.
Test for stationarity, interpret autocorrelation and partial autocorrelation functions and transform a series to stationarity.
Identify, estimate and diagnose ARIMA and seasonal ARIMA models and use them to forecast.
Evaluate forecasts with appropriate accuracy measures and time series cross-validation and choose between models.
Build and communicate a forecasting system for rainfall, prices or demand that decision makers can act on.

units.title: Time series data and components
topics: What makes time series different: dependence, ordering and the forecasting horizon
Time plots, seasonal plots, subseries plots, lag plots and scatter-plot matrices
Components: trend, seasonality, cycles and irregular variation; additive and multiplicative structure
Calendar effects, missing observations, irregular sampling and resampling to a common frequency
Handling time series in pandas: datetime indexes, rolling windows and resampling

units.title: Smoothing and decomposition
topics: Moving averages: simple, centred and weighted; moving averages of moving averages
Classical additive and multiplicative decomposition
STL decomposition with LOESS; robustness to outliers
Seasonal adjustment and its uses in official statistics (X-13ARIMA-SEATS in brief)
Box-Cox and log transformations; adjusting for inflation, population and calendar days
Decomposing monthly rainfall at Tamale into trend and seasonal patterns

units.title: Benchmark forecasts and exponential smoothing
topics: Benchmark methods: mean, naive, seasonal naive and drift; residual diagnostics
Simple exponential smoothing; choosing the smoothing parameter by minimising errors
Holt's linear trend and damped trend methods
Holt-Winters additive and multiplicative seasonal methods
The ETS state space framework: error, trend and seasonal combinations, likelihood and AIC
Prediction intervals and why they widen with the horizon

units.title: Stationarity and autocorrelation
topics: Strict and weak stationarity; white noise and random walks
The autocorrelation function and partial autocorrelation function; correlograms
Differencing and seasonal differencing; unit roots
Unit root and stationarity tests: augmented Dickey-Fuller and KPSS
Portmanteau tests for residual autocorrelation: Box-Pierce and Ljung-Box

units.title: ARIMA models
topics: The backshift operator; autoregressive AR(p) and moving average MA(q) processes
ARMA processes: stationarity and invertibility conditions; theoretical ACF and PACF patterns
ARIMA(p,d,q): model identification by the Box-Jenkins approach
Estimation by maximum likelihood; information criteria AIC, AICc and BIC; automatic order selection
Diagnostic checking of residuals and forecasting from ARIMA models
Modelling the monthly price of a bag of maize in Kumasi

units.title: Seasonal models and regression with time series
topics: Seasonal ARIMA models: (p,d,q)(P,D,Q)m notation, identification and fitting
Time series regression: trend and seasonal dummies, Fourier terms for long or multiple seasonality
Dynamic regression with ARIMA errors; lagged predictors and spurious regression
Interventions and outliers: level shifts, pulses and holiday effects such as Ramadan and Christmas trading
Multiple seasonality in hourly and daily data; an overview of TBATS and Prophet
Forecasting daily mobile money transaction volumes with weekly and monthly patterns

units.title: Forecast evaluation
topics: Training and test sets for time series; why random splitting fails
Point accuracy measures: MAE, RMSE, MAPE and its problems, and the scaled MASE
Evaluating distributions: prediction interval coverage, Winkler score and CRPS
Time series cross-validation with a rolling origin
Comparing models and the Diebold-Mariano test; forecast combination

units.title: Forecasting rainfall, prices and demand
topics: Rainfall forecasting for farmers in the north: onset dates, dry spells and seasonal totals
Market price forecasting for traders and food security monitoring; forecasting with sparse market data
Demand forecasting for inventory: hierarchical series, reconciliation and intermittent demand with Croston's method
Machine learning for time series in brief: lag features, gradient boosting and recurrent networks
Communicating forecasts and uncertainty to non-specialists; scenario forecasts
Capstone: a forecasting study on a Ghanaian series with model comparison and a written brief

schedule.title: Looking at time series
schedule.exercise: Describe the trend, seasonality and irregular variation you see in a monthly rainfall plot, and say how you would handle three missing months.

tasks.title: Plot monthly rainfall for 10 years as a time plot, a seasonal plot and a lag plot and describe what each reveals
Resample daily mobile money transactions to weekly and monthly totals with pandas and compute 7-day rolling means
Compare filling five missing months in a price series by interpolation, seasonal mean and forward fill, and measure the effect on later results

schedule.title: Smoothing and decomposition
schedule.exercise: Compute a centred 12-month moving average by hand for six months of data and explain why the end points are lost.

tasks.title: Compute 3, 5 and 12 point moving averages of a monthly series and plot them to see how window size changes smoothness
Decompose a monthly series additively and multiplicatively, compare the residuals and decide which structure fits better
Apply STL with different seasonal windows to a series with outliers, then compare robust and non-robust fits on the trend

schedule.title: Adjustments and transformations
schedule.exercise: Explain when a log transform stabilises a seasonal amplitude and when inflation adjustment is needed before analysis.

tasks.title: Apply a log and a Box-Cox transform to a series with growing seasonal swings and compare the variance of each seasonal cycle
Adjust a monthly price series for inflation and for days in the month, and show how the apparent growth changes
Decompose 20 years of monthly Tamale rainfall, estimate the seasonal peak month and test for a trend in the annual totals

schedule.title: Benchmarks and exponential smoothing
schedule.exercise: Compute naive, seasonal naive and drift forecasts for a short series by hand and check which has the smallest error.

tasks.title: Produce mean, naive, seasonal naive and drift forecasts for a 12-month holdout and compare their errors in a table
Fit simple exponential smoothing with alpha values 0.1 to 0.9 and pick the one with the lowest squared error, plotting the fits
Compare Holt's linear and damped trend methods on a series that flattens, and show the damped version's forecasts stay realistic

schedule.title: Seasonal smoothing and ETS
schedule.exercise: Explain why prediction intervals from a trending model widen with the horizon, and interpret one interval for a manager.

tasks.title: Fit additive and multiplicative Holt-Winters models to monthly sales and choose the one with the lower holdout error
Fit all valid ETS error, trend and seasonal combinations to a series and rank them by AICc, then check the winner's residuals
Simulate 1000 future paths from a fitted ETS model, compute empirical prediction intervals and compare coverage with the analytic ones

schedule.title: Stationarity and autocorrelation

tasks.title: Plot the ACF and PACF of white noise, a random walk and a seasonal series and describe what each pattern shows
Difference a trending series once and seasonally once, check the correlograms after each step and decide the order needed
Run ADF and KPSS tests on six series, reconcile any disagreement between them and settle on a differencing plan with Ljung-Box checks

schedule.title: ARMA and ARIMA models

tasks.title: Simulate AR(1) with phi 0.8 and MA(1) with theta 0.6, then compare their sample correlograms with the theoretical shapes
Check stationarity and invertibility of five ARMA parameter sets by finding the roots of their polynomials relative to the unit circle
Apply the Box-Jenkins identification steps to a differenced series, propose two candidate orders and justify them from the correlograms

schedule.title: Fitting and forecasting with ARIMA
schedule.exercise: Compare AIC and BIC choices for three ARIMA orders and explain why they might disagree.

tasks.title: Fit five ARIMA orders to one series and tabulate AIC, AICc and BIC to pick the best order
Check the residuals of a fitted ARIMA with a correlogram, normality plot and Ljung-Box test, and refit if the checks fail
Model monthly maize prices in Kumasi with ARIMA, forecast 12 months with intervals and compare the result against a naive benchmark

schedule.title: Seasonal ARIMA and regression
schedule.exercise: Write the equation of a (1,1,1)(0,1,1)12 model in backshift notation and explain each term.

tasks.title: Fit a seasonal ARIMA to monthly electricity or rainfall data, read its coefficients and forecast the next 12 months
Fit a regression with trend, seasonal dummies and Fourier terms and compare the fits for 2, 4 and 6 Fourier pairs by AICc
Show spurious regression between two random walks, then fix it with differencing or ARIMA errors and test the lagged predictor properly

schedule.title: Interventions and multiple seasonality
schedule.exercise: Explain how holiday trading periods and a regulatory fee change would enter a model for mobile money volumes.

tasks.title: Add a pulse dummy for a holiday and a step dummy for a tariff change to a regression, and read the estimated effects
Fit weekly plus annual Fourier terms to daily data and compare the forecasts with a model that uses only weekly seasonality
Forecast daily mobile money volumes with weekly and monthly patterns, handle holiday outliers and report 28-day forecast accuracy

tasks.title: Compute MAE, RMSE, MAPE and MASE for two forecast sets on a worked example and say which one ranks them differently and why

Compare two models with the Diebold-Mariano test and test whether averaging their forecasts beats both, with prediction interval coverage

schedule.title: Forecasting in practice in Ghana

tasks.title: Identify the rainy-season onset date each year from daily rainfall and plot how the date varies across 15 years
Forecast weekly tomato prices from sparse market data using seasonal naive and ETS, and judge the results against a simple rule
Forecast intermittent demand for spare parts with Croston's method, reconcile a two-level hierarchy of shops and compare against naive

schedule.title: Machine learning, communication and capstone
schedule.exercise: Draft a one-page brief for a non-specialist that states a forecast, its uncertainty and two scenarios, avoiding jargon.

tasks.title: Build lag features for a monthly series, fit a gradient boosting model and compare its holdout error with seasonal naive

Run a forecasting study on a Ghanaian series comparing four models by rolling-origin error and write a short brief with recommendations
